note: Noted by hand while choosing subject areas; each entry links the talk-page revision read. Banners and notices are edited over time, so a later revision may differ.

notes.fact: The talk pages of Liberalism and Classical liberalism carry the banner of WikiProject Libertarianism. There is no WikiProject Liberalism, so this project's liberalism coverage comes from the Libertarianism banner.

Neither talk page carries the WikiProject Philosophy banner. Postmodernism carries the banners of WikiProjects Culture, Skepticism and Visual arts; Michel Foucault those of Socialism and Libertarianism, among others. Neither fits a subject area here, so Michel Foucault is listed under socialism by his banner and Postmodernism is added on request.
The article Antisemitism carries no contentious-topic notice, while New antisemitism carries the Arab–Israeli one. Wikipedia's only contentious topic named for antisemitism is Antisemitism in Poland.
Wikipedia's Antisemitism in Poland notice also sits on Adolf Hitler, Auschwitz concentration camp and other Second World War and Holocaust articles, so that area is wider than its name.
The article Holocaust denial carries no contentious-topic notice. Its banners include WikiProjects Alternative views and Skepticism.

Far-right politics, Fascism and White nationalism carry no contentious-topic notice. Alt-right and Great Replacement conspiracy theory carry the US politics notice, and Alt-right also the banner of WikiProject Presidents of the United States.

Critical theory and Cultural Marxism conspiracy theory carry the WikiProject Socialism banner, so they fall in the socialism subject; the second also carries the Conservatism banner, so it falls in both.

notes.about: Buildings, figures, religions and campaigns filed as organisations (Wikidata)
notes.fact: Wikidata's classes place Hagia Sophia, the Dome of the Rock, Cain and Abel, Sharia, Muslims, the Spanish Inquisition and Persecution of Uyghurs in China under organisation, so they appear in the Islam list's organisations. In the China list the same happens to Buddhism (through “major religious group”) and the Great Leap Forward (through “campaign”). No rule moves them: they are kept as Wikidata files them, because a rule for buildings, religions and campaigns would need its own class list and would move other articles too. If such a rule is added, this note and the Categories page will give its date and the articles it moves.

The Shakers and Peoples Temple are recorded in Wikidata as movements as well as organisations, with no headquarters, chairperson or member count, so under this project's movement rule they are placed with ideas and movements.
The talk pages of Jesus, Rita Hayworth, MF Doom, Cat Stevens and Balinese Hinduism carry the WikiProject Islam banner, so they are in the Islam subject.
The talk pages of Dark Enlightenment and New World Order conspiracy theory carry the WikiProject Socialism banner, so they are in the socialism subject.

notes.about: Events filed as organisations through Wikidata's class chains
notes.fact: Following Wikidata's 'subclass of' links upward, several events and practices reach organisation, so they are placed among organisations: Gaza genocide and Armenian genocide (ethnic cleansing or ethnic violence > ethnic conflict > ethnic movement > political movement > social movement > group action > informal organization > organization); Nakba (forced displacement > population transfer > human migration > animal migration > migration > group action > informal organization > organization); Persecution of Uyghurs in China (political campaign > organization); Gamergate (social media campaign > media campaign > campaign > organization); Kleptocracy (form of government > organization). They are kept as Wikidata files them.

evidence.page: Wikidata: Persecution of Uyghurs in China

notes.about: The libertarianism flag on WikiProject Politics banners
notes.fact: Wikipedia's Libertarianism articles are those whose WikiProject Politics banner has libertarianism=yes. The talk pages of Socialism, Communism, Sharia, The Jerusalem Post and Kleptocracy carry that flag, so they are in the Libertarianism subject.

notes.about: WikiProject Conservatism banners on newspapers and a TV channel
notes.fact: The talk pages of The Times of India, The Economic Times and Hallmark Channel carry the WikiProject Conservatism banner, so they are among the Conservatism subject's news outlets.

notes.about: WikiProject China banners on American and Russian leaders and on wars elsewhere
notes.fact: The talk pages of Bill Clinton, Joseph Stalin and Katie Zacharia (a White House press secretary) carry the WikiProject China banner; Ronald Reagan and Nicholas II carry the WikiProject Asia banner with its china=yes flag, which places them in the same category. World War II, the Vietnam War and the Mali War also carry the WikiProject China banner. So all are in the China, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Tibet subject, several near the top by readership.

notes.about: Trading companies under the Hong Kong and Taiwan banners
notes.fact: The East India Company's talk page carries the WikiProject Hong Kong banner and the Dutch East India Company's the WikiProject Taiwan banner, so both are among the China subject's organisations.

notes.about: A university ranking filed as media (Wikidata)
notes.fact: Wikidata records the Academic Ranking of World Universities as an instance of magazine as well as a university ranking, so it is among the China subject's news outlets and media. It is kept as Wikidata files it.
